content.user_title: Audit Paid Conversion Tracking Before Launch
content.value_statement: Broken events and inconsistent attribution can distort campaign decisions. This skill checks conversion signals and produces a launch checklist with UTM and event specifications.
actual_capabilities: Checks conversion events against a user-run test and GA4 Conversions export.
Reviews UTM coverage, casing, vocabulary, and auto-tagging conflicts.
Builds a reusable UTM naming convention and conversion-event specification.
Gates deduplication rules and attribution-window alignment across advertising platforms.
Flags offline conversion gaps and modeled iOS-ATT measurement.
limitations: Requires user-provided exports and a manual test conversion for evidence.
Does not access advertising, pixel, tag-manager, or analytics APIs by default.
Does not reconcile order-level attribution or quantify incrementality.
Does not score account quality or design campaign structure.

use_cases.title: Validate a campaign launch
use_cases.description: Review event firing, UTM tags, deduplication, and attribution settings before paid traffic begins.

use_cases.title: Standardize measurement rules
use_cases.description: Create consistent UTM names and event definitions for teams managing several advertising platforms.

use_cases.title: Diagnose reporting differences
use_cases.description: Identify likely tagging, attribution-window, and modeled-data causes behind differences between GA4 and platform reports.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic pre-flight
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my conversion tracking before launch. Platforms: [platforms]. Conversion actions: [actions]. Mark each checklist item pass, fail, or needs-input.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a structured launch review.

prompt_templates.title: Build a tracking specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a UTM naming convention and conversion-event specification for [campaign]. Include source, medium, campaign, content, event names, values, currency, and deduplication IDs.
prompt_templates.scenario: A campaign team needs shared implementation rules.

prompt_templates.title: Review GA4 evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my GA4 Conversions and Traffic-acquisition exports for [platforms]. Check the manual test conversion, UTM consistency, event values, and source attribution.
prompt_templates.scenario: An analyst has exports and wants evidence-based findings.

prompt_templates.title: Assess cross-platform readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit measurement readiness across [platforms]. Gate deduplication ownership, attribution-window alignment, currency, timezone, offline imports, and iOS-ATT modeled gaps. List exact launch blockers.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team needs a cross-platform go or no-go assessment.

output_examples.input: Meta purchase events appear in GA4, but no manual test conversion was completed.
output: Test conversion: needs-input. Complete one purchase and confirm its event name, value, currency, transaction ID, source, and medium.
Launch status: fix first until end-to-end evidence is available.

output_examples.input: Paid links use Google, google, cpc, and ppc values for the same campaign.
output: UTM consistency: fail. Standardize the source as google and the medium as cpc.
Update affected links and verify that GA4 no longer splits traffic across duplicate rows.

output_examples.input: Google and Meta use different attribution windows, while GA4 order IDs are the declared source of truth.
output: Source of truth: pass. GA4 order IDs are declared for deduplication.
Attribution alignment: fail. Choose a common comparison window before launch.
Route order-level matching and overlap quantification to attribution reconciliation.

best_practices: Provide current GA4 exports and identify every platform and conversion action in scope.
Run one real test conversion and verify its event name, value, currency, source, and deduplication ID.
Use one lowercase UTM vocabulary and document attribution windows, currency, and timezone.
anti_patterns: Do not mark missing evidence as a pass.
Do not place names, email addresses, or order details in UTM parameters.
Do not compare platform conversion totals before aligning attribution windows and deduplication rules.

faq.question: Does this skill connect directly to GA4 or advertising platforms?
faq.answer: No. It works from user-provided exports and a manual test unless optional connectors are available.

faq.question: What evidence should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide GA4 Conversions and Traffic-acquisition exports, platform names, conversion actions, and one manual test conversion.

faq.question: Can it fix duplicate conversions?
faq.answer: It can define and gate a deduplication rule. It does not perform order-level reconciliation or quantify overlap.

faq.question: Does it create a UTM standard?
faq.answer: Yes. It defines source, medium, campaign, content, and term rules with consistent lowercase values.

faq.question: How are iOS-ATT modeled conversions handled?
faq.answer: Modeled or partial conversions are flagged for interpretation. They are not treated as failures when verifiable data exists.

faq.question: When is tracking launch-ready?
faq.answer: Tracking is launch-ready when no checklist item fails, required evidence is present, and modeled-data flags are acknowledged.
